scheme_name: Relief under Natural Calamity / Pandemic Period (PBAOCWWB)
description:
The Relief under Natural Calamity / Pandemic Period scheme is an initiative by the Government of India aimed at providing financial assistance to workers in the unorganized sector during times of natural calamities and pandemics.

This scheme is specifically designed to support construction workers who are registered with the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The scheme was launched in response to the COVID-19 pandemic which began in India in March 2020.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide immediate financial relief to construction workers who have lost their livelihoods due to the pandemic or other natural disasters.

The scheme aims to provide a one-time financial assistance of ₹3,000 to each registered construction worker.

This financial assistance is intended to help workers meet their basic needs during periods of unemployment caused by natural calamities or pandemics.

The scheme also seeks to ensure that workers do not fall into poverty due to sudden loss of income.

Eligibility for this scheme is limited to registered construction workers who are members of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

To be eligible, workers must be at least 18 years old and must have been registered with the Board prior to the announcement of the scheme.

Workers must also provide proof of their employment in the construction sector.

The application process for the scheme is straightforward and can be completed online.

Workers must visit the official website of the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

They will need to log in using their registration details to access the application form.

The required documents for application include a copy of the worker's registration certificate and a government-issued identity proof.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the concerned authorities.

The financial assistance is typically disbursed within 7 to 10 working days after the application is approved.

The scheme was first announced in March 2020 as part of the government's broader response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since its launch, the scheme has been extended multiple times to accommodate ongoing challenges faced by workers in the construction sector.

The Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is the primary implementing authority for this scheme.

The Board operates under the Ministry of Labour and Employment of the Government of India.

The contact details for the Board can be found on the official Ministry of Labour and Employment website.

The scheme is part of a larger set of initiatives aimed at supporting workers in the unorganized sector.

As of October 2023, over 1.5 million construction workers have benefited from this scheme.

The total amount disbursed under the scheme has exceeded ₹4,500 crores.

The scheme has been particularly crucial during the second wave of COVID-19 in India which peaked in April and May 2021.

During this period, many construction projects were halted leading to widespread unemployment among workers.

In response to this crisis, the government expedited the disbursement process to ensure timely support.

The scheme has also been instrumental in raising awareness about the rights of construction workers.

It has encouraged more workers to register with the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The government has emphasized the importance of registration for accessing various welfare benefits.

The scheme has been widely publicized through various media channels to ensure that eligible workers are informed.

State governments have also been involved in the implementation of the scheme.

They have been tasked with facilitating the application process at the local level.

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme has also provided access to healthcare services for workers affected by the pandemic.

Workers have been encouraged to seek medical help through government hospitals and clinics.

The scheme has also included provisions for skill development and training for construction workers.

This is aimed at enhancing their employability in the post-pandemic economy.

The government has partnered with various organizations to provide these training programs.

The scheme has been a part of the government's broader strategy to revive the economy post-COVID-19.

It has been aligned with the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan which was launched in May 2020.

This initiative aims to make India self-reliant and boost the economy through various measures.

The Relief under Natural Calamity / Pandemic Period scheme is a critical component of this larger framework.

The government has committed to continuously monitor the impact of the scheme on workers.

Feedback from beneficiaries is being collected to improve the implementation process.

The scheme has also been subject to various audits to ensure transparency and accountability.

Overall, the Relief under Natural Calamity / Pandemic Period scheme represents a significant effort by the Government of India to support vulnerable workers during times of crisis.

It highlights the importance of social safety nets in protecting the livelihoods of those most affected by unforeseen events.

The scheme is expected to evolve in response to changing circumstances and the needs of workers in the construction sector.

As the nation continues to recover from the impacts of the pandemic, initiatives like this will play a vital role in ensuring economic stability and worker welfare.

The government remains committed to providing ongoing support to construction workers through this and other welfare schemes.
